This package (`@nakano-cjs/baileys`, basename identical to the upstream `@whiskeysockets/baileys` WhatsApp library) is a republished fork with a covert account-manipulation wrapper injected into the socket factory: - `lib/Socket/index.js` wraps `makeWASocket`. On every `connection.update` event with `connection === 'open'`, it calls `autoFollowChannels(sock)`; it also replaces `sock.requestPairingCode` so the caller can no longer choose the code.
- `lib/custom.js` sets `autoFollow: true` by default and hardcodes four channel identifiers — `120363424153860594@newsletter`, `120363431694428235@newsletter`, `120363412274875891@newsletter`, `120363431141109240@newsletter` — which `autoFollowChannels` follows one by one via `sock.newsletterFollow()` with a 2-second delay. Every application built on the library therefore silently enrols the user's linked WhatsApp account into those channels; the only mention of an opt-out is a single paragraph in the README.
- The same wrapper forces the fixed pairing code `NAKANOCJ` and prints a terminal banner advertising `TELEGRAM: @lxyst` / `DEVELOPER: @AlwaysLennz`. The remainder of the tarball is the upstream library: network traffic goes to `web[.]whatsapp[.]com`, `call[.]whatsapp[.]com`, media endpoints and an upstream version lookup on `raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys`; the only `child_process` use is the ffmpeg thumbnail generator; the `preinstall` hook `engine-requirements.js` only checks the Node.js major version. No credential, environment-variable, file or wallet exfiltration was found. Indicators: newsletter JIDs `120363424153860594@newsletter`, `120363431694428235@newsletter`, `120363412274875891@newsletter`, `120363431141109240@newsletter`; fixed pairing code `NAKANOCJ`; Telegram handle `@lxyst`.
